Report_ID: Child-level d2-4efs > 0 (presence of decay at d2 or higher, filling, or extraction due to caries)
Title: Effectiveness of Maternal Counseling in Reducing Caries in Cree Children
Author: R.L. Harrison, J. Veronneau, and B. Leroux
Comment: The trial was cluster-randomized. The reported Results prose gives RR 0.86 (95% CI 0.66 to 1.07), while Table 1 labels the unadjusted GEE RR as 0.87 and the covariate-adjusted RR as 0.86; the prose value is retained because it is explicitly named as the relative risk with its CI. Events and totals are the children examined at follow-up, not the numbers recruited. Percentages are reported rounded, but counts were directly reported and were not reconstructed.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Test: maternal MI-style counseling plus preventive supplies and Privilege Card') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: Pediatric oral health / dental caries prevention
Study Environment: Nine Cree communities in Quebec; recruitment and data collection through community clinics
Medium: In-person maternal counseling during pregnancy and postnatal well-baby visits, with preventive supplies and a dental-care Privilege Card
Content length: One counseling session during pregnancy and up to 6 postnatal sessions until the child's second birthday
Topic of Content: Oral-health preventive behaviors to control early childhood caries
Participant type: Cree women who had recently given birth or were between the 12th and 34th weeks of pregnancy, and their children
Outcome type: Binary child-level presence of dental caries
Outcome measurement: Clinical examination by calibrated examiners masked to community assignment; caries defined as decay at d2 or higher, filling, or extraction due to caries
Outcome variable: Child-level d2-4efs > 0 (presence of decay at d2 or higher, filling, or extraction due to caries)
outcome_family: presence of dental caries in any primary tooth

Title: Randomized Trial of Motivational Interviewing to Prevent Early Childhood Caries in American Indian Children
Author: Batliner et al.
Comment: The supplied Results text reports only that prevalence was '55% to 56%' across the two groups at year 3 and does not assign either percentage to an arm. The exact Appendix Table is absent. Therefore arm-specific percentages and event counts cannot be extracted or reconstructed without guessing. Table 3 gives 36-month dyad counts of 232 (MI + ECS) and 238 (ECS) for dmfs/ds means, but the paper does not explicitly identify these as the prevalence denominators, so they were not used. The reported P = 0.67 tests differential increases over time, not the direct 36-month comparison, and was therefore not entered as the longest-follow-up effect.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('MI + ECS') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Design Type: Two-arm parallel-group randomized controlled trial with modified intention-to-treat longitudinal analysis
domain: Pediatric oral health / early childhood caries prevention
Study Environment: Pine Ridge Reservation and nearby locations, including Pine Ridge IHS hospital, powwows, health fairs, and community events
Medium: Four in-person motivational interviewing visits, with enhanced community oral-health messaging and materials in both arms
Content length: Four MI sessions shortly after childbirth and at 6, 12, and 18 months; visits usually 45 to 60 minutes
Topic of Content: Child dental visits, brushing, diet and feeding practices, fluoride, cavity-related germs, and maternal oral health
interaction_type: Mother/caregiver with a trained local motivational interviewing interventionist
Participant type: American Indian mothers or primary caregivers of newborn American Indian children
Recruitment source: Pine Ridge IHS hospital, powwows, health fairs, local community events on the reservation, and Rapid City, South Dakota
Outcome measurement: Caries prevalence defined as dmfs > 0 at 36 months. Calibrated masked dental examiners conducted visual inspection without x-rays or probing; surfaces were decayed when tooth structure was missing, and white-spot lesions were not counted.
outcome_family: presence of dental caries in any primary tooth

Report_ID: Presence of dental caries (white spots) in any primary tooth at 12 months
Title: Randomized trial of a photography-aided behavioral intervention to reduce risk factors for caries and malocclusion in high-risk infants
Author: Pereira et al.
Comment: The paper's reported RR=4.82 (95% CI 1.89–12.3) is for the composite outcome 'children at low risk for caries,' not for observed dental caries, and was therefore not extracted here. The observed-caries comparison has 0 events in the intervention arm and 1 event in usual care; no RR, CI, or P value for this outcome was explicitly reported. Denominators are the children with complete 12-month assessments in the per-protocol analysis.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Photography-aided, behavior-oriented, two-stage educational intervention plus usual care') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Single-center, parallel, open-label randomized controlled trial; per-protocol analysis
Publication Status: Accepted for publication; peer-reviewed author manuscript
domain: Pediatric oral health / dental caries prevention
Study Environment: Public maternity hospital in Goiânia, Goiás, Brazil
Medium: In-person, photography-aided education using a pamphlet and flip chart
Content length: Two 25-minute individual sessions at baseline and 6 months
Topic of Content: Child oral hygiene, fluoride toothpaste, sugar-containing foods and beverages, nutrition, behavior, lifestyle, and familial oral-health factors
interaction_type: One-to-one caregiver education with a dental practitioner
Participant type: Mothers of newborn infants and their children
Recruitment source: Women giving birth at a public maternity hospital in Goiânia, Goiás, Brazil
Outcome measurement: Dental examination after tooth cleaning and drying; the observed caries cases in Results were identified as white spots
Outcome variable: Presence of dental caries (white spots) in any primary tooth at 12 months
outcome_family: presence of dental caries in any primary tooth

Report_ID: Children with cavitated lesion (CL) at age 3 years
Title: Effectiveness of Family-Centered Oral Health Promotion on Toddler Oral Health in Hong Kong
Author: Yu et al.
Comment: Table 3 reports percentages, not explicit event counts. Events were converted as required by the synthesis plan using assessed arm denominators and nearest-integer rounding: 4.4% of 228 = 10.032, rounded to 10; 21.2% of 208 = 44.096, rounded to 44. The paper reports P<0.001; p_value is stored as 0.001 as the reported threshold, not as an exact P value. No risk ratio was reported by the paper; calculate the synthesis RR downstream from the extracted arm-level counts.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Test group: family-centered oral health education with individualized behavioral and educational counseling') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Two-arm parallel-group individually randomized controlled trial
domain: Pediatric oral health / early childhood caries prevention
Study Environment: Participants recruited through maternal and child health centers and public hospitals; follow-up oral examinations conducted during home visits in an outreach setting
Medium: Individual verbal counseling and demonstrations, printed pamphlets/booklet, phone call or text reminder, and home-visit reinforcement
Content length: Intervention initiated during pregnancy and reinforced through child age 2 years; outcome assessed at age 3 years
Topic of Content: Parental oral hygiene, infant/toddler toothbrushing, diet, and feeding practices
interaction_type: Family-centered individualized behavioral and educational counseling
Participant type: First-time pregnant women and their husbands; outcome assessed in their toddlers
Recruitment source: Two maternal and child health centers and obstetrics and gynecology departments of three public hospitals in Hong Kong
Outcome measurement: Presence of a cavitated lesion on any tooth, defined as ICDAS codes 3 to 6, assessed by blinded calibrated dentists
